$comment: The source of sf-close's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/close (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet, so a second copy of the markup would only drift from the one that draws.

x-summary: The decorative cross glyph of a close action, sized on the control ladder. It is aria-hidden and never focusable; the containing native button owns the action and its name.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-close only as the decorative cross glyph inside a host-owned close action.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component
Do not make sf-close focusable or use it as the action owner
ai_guidance.minimal_example: <button type="button" class="sf-icon-button sf-icon-button--close sf-icon-button--link sf-icon-button--on-surface sf-icon-button--size-1 flex items-cross-center" aria-label="Close notification"><sf-close size="1"></sf-close></button>

x-decisions: a11y-role: none. The cross is decorative and drawn aria-hidden; it is never focusable. The native button it stands in (an icon button) owns the role, the name, focus and the dismiss effect.
a11y-name: none (the old shape "internal" meant the same): the glyph has no name of its own; the containing button carries aria-label.
template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows; no template.html until the build compiles one (a copy nothing draws would drift).
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json (size 1) plus the default 1/3, the smallest 1/4 and the largest 7, and the glyph inside a native icon button.

css-variables: five public variables (glyph colour, background, glyph size, padding inline and block), read by the class sheet with the role token as fallback (§6) and listed in src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json.
version 1.0.0: the interface is unchanged (size alone); nothing is renamed, so aliases.json is empty.
